subject: Streaming Latency Surge — Temporary Bridging Plan & Next Steps
summary: Customer reported elevated latency on streaming/chat endpoints during a 30-minute window. We implemented a temporary bridging rule to route traffic to lower-latency edge. Investigation points to a hotspike in one regional shard combined with suboptimal KV-cache eviction under a specific token pattern. Short-term mitigations applied; permanent fixes scheduled.

Hi Samira —

Sharing the quick mitigations you can apply immediately (SDK + HTTP clients):
1) Fallback routing: enable our client header X-Redwood-Prefer-Edge: true to prefer lower-latency edge nodes (no code change for standard SDKs — see snippet below).
2) Timeout: set streaming read timeout to 1500ms and implement a jittered exponential reconnect (100ms -> 300ms -> 900ms).
3) Prompt hygiene: temporarily remove the 3rd-party prefix if you can, or compress it into a single system message to reduce token repetition.

Example node snippet: 
// pseudo
const client = new Redwood({headers: {'X-Redwood-Prefer-Edge': 'true'}})
client.stream(..., {readTimeoutMs: 1500, reconnectStrategy: 'jitteredExponential'})

I'll also attach the bridging config we pushed (it routes 20% of traffic to alternate-edge and rebalances over 30m). We'll monitor and report at 15:00 PST.

Monica
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident update: root cause, short-term mitigations, and next steps

Hi Samira and Liam —

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Summary of findings and next steps below.

What happened (brief):
- Root cause: a combination of a token-pattern that forced repeated KV-cache entries for large conversation histories, and a software path in our shard allocator that did not rehydrate a hot KV bucket quickly after eviction. The result: increased compute per-token and token delivery delays concentrated on a single physical shard in us-west.

What we did:
- Short-term: enforced a routing bridge to healthy edges for GreenMark traffic and applied a cache-protect policy to reduce eviction churn.
- Medium-term: rolled an optimized KV rehydration patch to the shard (verified in staging) and scheduled a controlled restart for the affected shard during the customer's off-peak window (Nov 30, 23:00 PST).
- Long-term: planned changes include a more aggressive hot-key detection and shard fencing logic to avoid this class of events. Target delivery: Q1 2027.

Customer impact: ~12% of streaming sessions had 1–3s additional latency over a 31-minute window; no dropped messages and no data exposure. We observed a small increase in abandoned sessions for your live chat flows; we will discuss credits if impact materially affects your SLA.

Attachments: latency-traces-20261129.zip (full traces), bridging-config-runbook-v1.md (exact routing rules).

Proposed customer-facing remediation actions we recommend you apply now:
- Keep the X-Redwood-Prefer-Edge header enabled for 48 hours.
- Apply readTimeoutMs = 1500ms and reconnect strategy as recommended by Monica.
- Run a non-prod load test against the suggested routing header to validate behavior.

Follow-up plan:
- Nov 30, 23:00 PST: controlled shard restart (we will provide 30m notice).
- Dec 2: joint postmortem call (30 min) to walk findings and SLA remediation; we'll send calendar invite.

If you'd like, we can prepare a short customer-facing RCA format for your internal stakeholders.

Thanks again — we'll remain on standby during the restart and will share result telemetry immediately after.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
